name: Guinea-Bissau

findings.financier: Unclear: Ecofin says government-funded; Osiris says Huawei to invest
findings.summary: The government and Huawei signed a contract to rebuild state-owned Guiné Telecom's network with 150 powered telecom sites, aiming to relaunch it as the country's third mobile operator after it halted mobile service in 2014.

sources.publisher: OSIRIS (Observatoire sur les systèmes d'information, Senegal)

findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc: Huawei is the equipment vendor. Implementation is unverified and doubtful: DCD (Feb 2023) reports Guiné Telecom/Guinetel bankrupt since 2013, relicensed in 2021 for revival and offered for 80% sale; the finance minister said in 2022 the network is controlled by MTN and Orange. Possibly never built; still_current left null. Value is Ecofin's (FCFA 36bn); source dates approximate (Ecofin article id suggests 4 Jan 2016).

findings.local_actor: Government of Guinea-Bissau with Orange Bissau and MTN (now Telecel) consortium
findings.financier: World Bank (c. US$31.6m loan); Orange and MTN c. US$8m each
findings.summary: Guinea-Bissau's first submarine-cable connection, a roughly 30 km link from the ACE cable landing at Suru to Antula near Bissau, was completed and inaugurated in March 2023 under a US$47m World Bank-backed government–Orange–MTN project.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: no opened source names the equipment supplier for the landing link or Guinea-Bissau's ACE branch; Orange (France) and MTN are operator consortium partners, not vendors. Reviewer may set third if the supplier is confirmed (ACE system was built by a French supplier, not verified here). Ecofin (2025) says benefits remain mostly coastal pending a national backbone; Forbes cites EUR 30m World Bank funding.

findings.local_actor: President Umaro Sissoco Embaló / Ministry of Interior
findings.summary: The president promised surveillance cameras across all of Bissau from January 2025, extending cameras he ordered in parts of the capital in 2020 with monitoring at the Interior Ministry; no vendor, contract or funder was named.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: vendor unknown. Statement of intent only (tier 1). Whether the 2025 rollout happened, and who supplied the 2020 cameras, is unestablished.
